intro.text: Headquartered in Nassau, Bahamas, OneSpaWorld is one of the largest health and wellness services companies in the world. OneSpaWorld’s distinguished health and wellness centers offer guests a comprehensive suite of premium health, wellness, aesthetics and fitness services, treatments, and products, currently onboard 208 cruise ships and at 25 destination resorts around the world. OneSpaWorld holds the leading market position within the cruise industry segment of the international leisure market, which it has earned over six decades upon its exceptional service; expansive global recruitment, training and logistics platforms; irreplicable operating infrastructure; powerful team; and product innovation, delivering tens of millions of extraordinary guest experiences and outstanding service to its cruise line and destination resort partners.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our solution sales approach drives substantial retail product add on sales to complement our services offerings, with approximately 19% of our revenues derived from the sale of retail products during the year ended December 31, 2025.
Guests that received these customized promotions were responsible for approximately 11% of revenues generated during the year ended December 31, 2025.
During 2025, product sales comprised approximately 19% of our revenues, enabling incremental revenue even at full treatment room utilization.
However, OneSpaWorld (Maritime)’s shipboard income generated while in port in The Bahamas is subject to the payment of a 10% VAT payable to the Bahamas Department of Inland Revenue.

Total revenues increased 7% to $961.0 million compared to $895.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, principally driven by fleet expansion due to 2025 new ship builds, a 3% increase in average guest spend, and a 2% increase in revenue days contributing $27.9 million, $25.7 million, and $17.0 million, respectively, of the increase in Total revenues for the period, of which $10.7 million was attributable to increased guest pre-booked services.
As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, none of the destination resort spas we served represented greater than 10% of our accounts receivable.
As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, four and three, respectively, of the cruise lines we served represented greater than 10% of our accounts receivable.
As of December 31, 2025, and 2024, the Company had four and three cruise companies, respectively, that represented greater than 10 % of accounts receivable.

Cruise line and destination resort partners depend on us to provide their guests with the best and broadest assortment of services and products to enhance their vacation experience and the competitive positioning and consumer value of their brands.
Our success depends on our ability to recruit and train employees skilled in our customer service philosophy.

The success of our business relies on the devoted and experienced leadership of our cruise ship and destination resort health and wellness center managers and our corporate leaders, both senior executives and operational managers.
We Depend on Our Agreements with Cruise Lines and Destination Resort Health and Wellness Centers; if These Agreements Terminate, Our Business Would Be Harmed
We Depend on the Cruise Industry and Their Risks Are Risks to Us
According to CLIA, North America, our core market, continues to remain the largest source market for passenger volume.
We Depend on the Continued Viability of the Ships and Destination Resort Health and Wellness Centers We Serve

We depend on commercial airlines for the transportation of our shipboard employees to and from the ships we serve and, as a result, we pay for a relatively large number of flights for these employees each year.
We Depend on Our Key Officers and Qualified Employees
The Success of Health and Wellness Centers Depends on the Hospitality Industry
Our ability to meet our debt service obligations will depend on our future performance, which will be affected by the other risk factors described herein.

Our ability to provide certain additional services depends on our ability to find appropriate third parties with whom to work in connection with these services and, in certain cases, could be dependent on our ability to fund substantial costs.
We rely on a variety of direct marketing techniques, including telemarketing, email marketing, and direct mail.

There is limited judicial guidance from the courts of the Cayman Islands regarding the circumstances under which judgments obtained from U.S. courts under civil liability provisions of U.S. securities laws will be considered penal or punitive in nature; however, it will likely depend on the particular provision and the remedy sought.

The declaration and payment of future dividends to holders of our common shares is at the discretion of our Board and depends upon many factors, including our financial condition, earnings, capital requirements of our business, covenants associated with certain debt obligations, legal requirements, regulatory constraints, industry practice and other factors that our Board deems relevant.

The accounting for changes in the fair value of derivatives depends on the intended use of the derivative, whether the Company has elected to designate a derivative in a hedging relationship and apply hedge accounting and whether the hedging relationship has satisfied the criteria necessary to apply hedge accounting.
Fixed or minimum payments and variable lease payments that depend on a rate or index are included in the calculation of the right-of-use asset.
